title: Each microservice's internal endpoint rejects the WRONG internal-auth header name, not just a wrong value
description: The platform uses at least four different internal-auth header conventions across services: vibrantix-backend's /api/internal/notifications and the *-service BackendApiClient calls use 'X-Internal-Token'; risk-management-service's /internal/* routes (internal.routes.ts) use 'X-Internal-API-Key'; trust-vault-service's /s2s/* routes (s2s.routes.ts) use 'x-internal-service-token'; vibrantix-backend's audit-report-generator-service client uses 'x-service-token'. A caller that sends the CORRECT shared secret value under the WRONG header name for that particular service must still be rejected — this guards against a copy-paste integration bug where a new caller reuses another service's header name with a valid token value and silently 'works' due to permissive header parsing.
preconditions: Valid value of INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN/INTERNAL_API_TOKEN shared secret
steps: Call risk-management-service's POST /internal/vendor-risks/events with the correct token value under header 'X-Internal-Token' (backend's header name) instead of 'X-Internal-API-Key'
Call trust-vault-service's GET /s2s/certifications with the correct token value under header 'X-Internal-Token' instead of 'x-internal-service-token'
Call vibrantix-backend's POST /api/internal/notifications with the correct token value under header 'x-internal-service-token' instead of 'X-Internal-Token'
expectedResult: All three calls are rejected with 401 Unauthorized — none of the services accept a token under a header name other than their own documented one, and no service falls back to checking multiple header names for the same secret.

title: trust-vault-service's DEV_BYPASS flag cannot silently disable S2S token validation outside development
description: s2s.routes.ts's validateInternalToken() short-circuits to `true` (no token check at all) when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && process.env.DEV_BYPASS === 'true'`. If either env var is misconfigured in a staging/prod-like environment (e.g. NODE_ENV left as 'development' in a shared staging box that other services treat as trusted), every /s2s/* endpoint — including certification/report/incident listing across orgs — becomes unauthenticated.
preconditions: Access to set NODE_ENV and DEV_BYPASS env vars for a non-production trust-vault-service instance
steps: Set NODE_ENV=development and DEV_BYPASS=true on the target instance
Call GET /s2s/certifications with no X-Internal-Token/x-internal-service-token header at all and arbitrary vendorOrgId/partnerOrgId query params
Repeat with NODE_ENV=production (or DEV_BYPASS unset) and confirm the same unauthenticated call is now rejected
expectedResult: With the bypass conditions active, the endpoint responds without requiring the token (documenting the current bypass behavior as a configuration risk to be flagged); with either condition absent, the same unauthenticated call returns 401. Deployment configs for staging/production must never set both NODE_ENV=development and DEV_BYPASS=true.

title: BackendApiClient's circuit breaker opens after 5 consecutive 5xx responses and fails fast for 30 seconds
description: vendor-service's (and equivalent risk-management-service/trust-vault-service) BackendApiClient.ts implements a process-level circuit breaker: 2 retries with [200ms, 500ms] backoff on network error or 5xx, and after 5 consecutive 5xx responses it opens for 30s (CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RESET_MS), failing fast without hitting the network at all until the cool-down elapses.
preconditions: Ability to force vibrantix-backend to return 500 for a specific internal endpoint on demand
steps: Force the backend to return 500 for an endpoint BackendApiClient calls (e.g. /api/internal/pcl/events)
From vendor-service, trigger 5 consecutive calls that hit that endpoint
Immediately trigger a 6th call and measure whether it makes a network request at all
Wait 30+ seconds, restore the backend to 200, and trigger another call
expectedResult: Calls 1-5 each attempt the network request (with retry/backoff) and fail. Call 6 fails immediately with a 'Circuit breaker OPEN' error and does NOT reach the network (verifiable via absence of a new request in backend access logs). After the 30s cool-down and backend recovery, the next call succeeds and resets consecutiveFailures to 0.

title: project-scope-client and entitlement-client fail closed (503 / ProjectScopeUnavailableError) rather than granting unrestricted access when the backend is unreachable
description: Both shared clients (project-scope-client.cjs used by rs/vs/tv/cs/vciso/assistant, and entitlement-client.cjs) cache successfully-resolved values for a soft TTL (10s for project-scope, 60s for entitlements) and serve stale data up to a 5-minute hard expiry on RPC failure, then throw ProjectScopeUnavailableError / EntitlementUnavailableError (503) rather than defaulting to permissive access. This is a critical fail-closed guarantee for multi-tenant isolation.
preconditions: A microservice using project-scope-client (e.g. risk-management-service) with an empty cache for the target user/org pair
vibrantix-backend's /internal/users/:userId/projects endpoint made unreachable (stopped or network-partitioned)
steps: With no prior cache entry for (userId, organizationId), stop/block vibrantix-backend
Call an endpoint on risk-management-service that depends on getScope(userId, organizationId)
Restore backend connectivity, make one successful call to warm the cache, then immediately re-block backend and repeat the call within the 5-minute hard-expiry window
Wait past the 5-minute hard expiry with backend still blocked and repeat again
expectedResult: First call (cold cache, backend down): fails closed with a 503 ProjectScopeUnavailableError — never treated as 'unrestricted'. Second call (warm cache, backend down, within hard expiry): serves the last known-good scope from cache. Third call (past hard expiry, backend still down): fails closed again with 503.

title: RiskComplianceBridgeService's outbox delivers risk-control mapping events to the backend exactly once, and dead-letters after 20 failed attempts
description: risk-management-service enqueues 'risk_requirement_mapping_updated'/'risk_ucl_mapping_updated'/'risk_compliance_mapping_snapshot' events into a durable outbox (idempotent on a sha256 eventId of type+org+payload) and posts them to POST /api/internal/pcl/events with X-Internal-Token + X-Service-ID: risk-service. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff (15 * 2^attempts seconds, capped at 3600s) up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=20 before moving to 'dead_letter'.
preconditions: A risk with requirement/control mappings that can be changed
Ability to inspect the compliance_event_outbox collection directly
steps: Change a risk's requirement mapping (add and remove at least one requirement)
Immediately re-trigger the same exact mapping change again (identical added/removed sets) before the first event is confirmed delivered
Inspect the outbox collection for duplicate eventId entries
Force POST /api/internal/pcl/events to fail (backend down) and observe the outbox document's delivery.attempts and nextAttemptAt progression across retries
expectedResult: The duplicate identical mapping change does NOT create a second outbox document — the sha256-derived eventId collides and upsertedCount is 0 for the repeat. Under sustained backend failure, delivery.attempts increments and nextAttemptAt backs off exponentially (capped at 3600s) until attempts reaches 20, at which point delivery.status becomes 'dead_letter' with lastError populated, and the event stops being retried indefinitely.

title: connector-service's compliance event outbox marks superseded events correctly when a newer scan snapshot arrives before the prior one is delivered
description: ComplianceEventOutboxService's IntegrationComplianceEvent is 'authoritative: true' with an observedAt/validUntil window per integration+syncJobId. If a second scan for the same integration completes and enqueues a new snapshot before the first one's outbox entry has been delivered, the older entry must not later overwrite the newer control states once both eventually deliver out of order.
preconditions: An integration with two scans triggerable in close succession
Ability to delay/throttle outbox delivery to backend/risk-management-service artificially
steps: Trigger a cloud scan (syncJobId A) and artificially delay its Stage 7 outbox delivery
Before A's event delivers, trigger a second scan (syncJobId B) for the same integration and allow B's event to deliver normally
Allow A's delayed event to finally deliver
Check the compliance map's control states for controls covered by this integration
expectedResult: A's outbox entry is marked 'superseded' (not delivered as if authoritative) once B's later snapshot has already landed, OR the receiving side (backend/risk-management-service) rejects/ignores an out-of-order snapshot whose observedAt predates the currently-stored one for that integration — the compliance map never regresses to A's older, possibly-stale control states after B's newer ones were already applied.

title: trust-vault-service's /s2s/certifications response strips allowedPartnerIds/excludedPartnerIds regardless of which field name the frontend/partner client expects
description: s2s.routes.ts explicitly rebuilds a 'safeMeta' object for sharingMetadata (trustNetworkEnabled, minimumSharingLevel, includeDocument, customLabel [, redactedSummary for reports]) and deletes the raw sharingMetadata — this is a deliberate contract narrowing, not a bug, but any consuming client (vendor-service's Trust Network view) that still expects allowedPartnerIds/excludedPartnerIds on this response would silently receive undefined rather than an error. Confirms the actual wire shape matches what vendor-service's TrustNetworkService/consumer code expects.
preconditions: A certification with trustNetworkEnabled=true and non-empty allowedPartnerIds set for org A
A partner org B with S2S access
steps: Call GET /s2s/certifications?vendorOrgId=A&partnerOrgId=B directly and inspect the raw JSON response for the sharingMetadata object on a matching certification
Cross-check every field vendor-service's consumer of this endpoint actually reads against the fields present in the response
expectedResult: The response's sharingMetadata contains only trustNetworkEnabled, minimumSharingLevel, includeDocument, customLabel (never allowedPartnerIds/excludedPartnerIds); the calling code in vendor-service does not attempt to read the stripped fields and does not silently render 'undefined'/blank where a partner list might have been expected.

title: connector-service's compliance/risk event envelopes carry schemaVersion, and consumers reject or safely ignore an unrecognized future version
description: Both IntegrationComplianceEvent and RiskEventEnvelope declare a literal schemaVersion of '1.0'. As the platform evolves these envelopes, a consumer (backend's PCL ingestion, or risk-management-service's ingestion) must not blindly deserialize a future '2.0'-shaped payload as if it were '1.0' and silently corrupt or misinterpret fields.
preconditions: Ability to hand-craft/replay an outbox-shaped event payload directly against the ingestion endpoint
steps: Submit a hand-crafted event to the backend's PCL ingestion endpoint (or risk-management-service's ingestion) with schemaVersion set to an unrecognized value (e.g. '2.0') and a controlStates/facts shape that differs from '1.0'
Observe how the receiving service handles the unrecognized version
expectedResult: The consumer either explicitly rejects the payload with a clear 'unsupported schemaVersion' error, or has documented forward-compatibility handling — it must not attempt to interpret an unrecognized version's fields as if they were the '1.0' shape, which could corrupt control-state or risk data.
